To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

energy is a complex topic that has many different dimensions and that there are many opportunities for HCI to contribute to this field, especially in the areas of energy feedback displays, demand response, energy markets, and smart grid.

energy is an emerging topic of importance in HCI, that there is a cluster of research in the area of electricity consumption feedback, and that there is potential for HCI to engage more deeply with emerging energy systems.

energy-related HCI research has focused on ECF, that ECF research can be extended to other emerging systems, and that HCI can contribute to emerging systems by designing interactions that are more experientially meaningful and that better address the social aspects of energy systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people experience, understand, and engage with emerging energy systems.

the design of interaction, technology, and systems that can help individuals, communities, and society to engage with and manage the emerging energy systems that are increasingly shaping our everyday lives.

understanding how HCI can engage with the emerging energy systems landscape to create meaningful, useful, and usable experiences that support the adoption and use of energy systems technologies and practices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field of HCI is at a crossroads with respect to energy and sustainability.
the field of HCI has a great deal to contribute to the emerging energy systems of the future, and the future is now.
the field of HCI is in the early stages of engaging with the complex, multidisciplinary challenges associated with the design and deployment of emerging energy systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the emerging energy systems trends identified in this paper provide a number of opportunities for HCI researchers and practitioners to engage with energy and sustainability issues.
HCI research on energy has been dominated by ECF, but that the field should now look to engage with a wider range of emerging energy technologies, systems, and behaviors.
HCI has a unique opportunity to engage with the emerging energy systems and to design for their social and cultural aspects, as well as to explore how they will impact our everyday lives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HCI has a unique opportunity to contribute to the design and evaluation of emerging energy systems and their interaction with people and society.
HCI can make a significant impact by moving beyond energy monitors to explore the interaction and user experience challenges of new energy systems and technologies.
there is a great deal of opportunity for HCI to engage more deeply with energy and sustainability, particularly with the emerging systems that are currently being developed.
